artifact_revision: agentmux f0b8512d + session-11 working tree (amx 0.8.0 built from it into an isolated bin); stock Ghostty 1.3.2-main+c770410db; Kitty 0.49.1; tmux 3.7c on AgentMux's private server; installed asl 0.2.0; macOS 27.0.1
method: Live runs on this machine in an isolated world under /tmp/amxs11 (own HOME, TMPDIR, config, daemon, runtime-session registry, private tmux server), so the operator's Kitty, daemon, tmux, and config were never used. The surface under test is this checkout's amx. Ghostty: a new stock Ghostty process (--config-default-files=false) ran the dashboard; its screen was read and its keyboard driven through an observer tmux on a separate socket that hosts the surface inside the Ghostty window (Ghostty has no remote control), plus one run with nothing in between whose window was screenshotted. Kitty: a new, separate Kitty process (--config NONE, own --listen-on socket) was driven and read with kitten @ send-text/send-key/get-text/ls, with no observer. Every step waited for the expected text on screen and each log ends with its count of failed steps (all 0). Stand-ins, stated plainly: the harness is a shell script named claude (no model, no network) that prints its identity, emits real hooks through `amx hook-indicator` on typed commands, and, as an `asl run` worker, holds one turn open and completes its session; the editor is a script that prints and waits for enter. Real: Ghostty, Kitty, tmux, the amx dashboard/overview/hook client/daemon, the runtime-session registry, Git worktrees, and the installed asl with its hooks and bridge. Not exercised live: a real Claude/Codex/Copilot agent, physical keyboard input (keys were sent through tmux and kitten), and the color/icon pickers inside Kitty (unchanged code; their tests pass). The first two Kitty passes were discarded because Kitty starts launched tabs through login(1), which reset HOME and ran the real claude onboarding screen instead of the stand-in; the recorded pass isolates those tabs with a private ZDOTDIR. One line class in the Ghostty log is redacted (the zsh prompt's user@host).

ghostty-tmux-dashboard.evidence: In a stock Ghostty 1.3.2 window (client_termname=xterm-ghostty, TERM_PROGRAM=ghostty, no KITTY_LISTEN_ON) a bare `amx` started the dashboard with no Kitty client: 'No running sessions', then a launch from the launcher created one session on the private tmux server (registry: live, fresh, tmux %0) while the dashboard stayed up and showed the row with a live inspector preview read from the tmux pane. Enter attached the Ghostty window to the agent (one client on the private server), a PermissionRequest hook typed into the agent arrived as a managed hook, and F12 detached back to a dashboard showing 'Needs you (1) / Needs permission' for that row with zero clients left attached. `amx overview` in a second stock Ghostty window (130x40) showed both tmux sessions as tiles, live previews captured from the panes after `c`, attach on Enter, and F12 back. A third run with nothing between amx and Ghostty was screenshotted listing two tmux sessions with the inspector preview. 0 failed steps. Artifacts: session-11/ghostty-tmux-dashboard.log (W1-W3, W12), session-11/ghostty-direct-dashboard.png.

kitty-tmux-dashboard.evidence: In a separate real Kitty 0.49.1 instance, `amx --backend tmux` listed the already-running Kitty-backed session and, on launch, created beta on the private tmux server with no new Kitty tab (kitten @ ls unchanged; registry: live, fresh, tmux %0) while the dashboard stayed up showing both rows in one list. Selecting the tmux row filled the inspector from the tmux pane; Enter attached inside the Kitty window (private-server client xterm-kitty); a hook typed there and F12 returned to a dashboard showing beta (tmux) 'Needs permission' beside alpha (Kitty). Peek on the tmux row opened less in the dashboard's own window and created no Kitty overlay window. `amx overview --backend tmux` showed one Kitty tile and one tmux tile. A plain `amx` in Kitty listed both once the private server existed; closing the tmux row ended its server session and marked its runtime session ended, and closing the Kitty row removed its tab. 0 failed steps. Artifact: session-11/kitty-tmux-dashboard.log (T1-T5).

legacy-kitty-actions.evidence: In the same real Kitty instance with no --backend flag and no tmux server, the dashboard launched alpha as a new Kitty tab titled '🟠alpha' and quit (no tmux server, no runtime-session registry created). A legacy hook from that tab made the daemon retitle it '🔑🟠alpha'; the reopened dashboard listed it as 'Needs permission'. Through the actions menu, observed in kitten @ ls tab titles: Clear status -> '🟠alpha', Mark active -> '⚡🟠alpha', Lock -> '🔒⚡🟠alpha', Mute -> '🔒🔇⚡🟠alpha'; Peek opened the native Kitty overlay pager (a new window running less); Restart replaced the agent (tab 3/window 3 -> tab 4/window 5); Enter focused the agent's tab and the dashboard quit to the shell; `amx overview` showed the Kitty session tile. 0 failed steps. Existing Kitty acceptance in the suite still passes unchanged: TestRemoteControlBaseline and the Kitty backend contract (go test ./internal/kitty), the tui/overview acceptance suite, and all 157 pre-existing TUI scenarios. Artifact: session-11/legacy-kitty-actions.log (L1-L9).

portable-workflow-matrix.evidence: Each workflow observed on screen in stock Ghostty with no Kitty, in session-11/ghostty-tmux-dashboard.log: launching (W2: launcher -> tmux session, dashboard stays); focus and state (W3: attach, managed hook, F12); session actions (W4: clear status, mark active (Working), lock (🔒 on the row, amx_locked=true in pane metadata) and mute (cc_mute=1 in pane metadata); W6: restart recorded as relation restart with the old runtime session ended; W11: close ends the record); utility views in place of Kitty overlays and tabs (W4: scrollback in less, shell printing SHELL_UTILITY_VIEW in the project directory, stand-in editor 'EDITOR VIEW', each returning to the dashboard); capability-aware actions (W5: Resort Tabs 'Unavailable: there are no Kitty tabs to reorder'; W13: color-picker and icon-picker refuse outside Kitty with exit status 1); history and continuity (W7: Past Sessions listed the conversation, continue resumed it on tmux with `--resume 11111111-...`, and continuing it again attached to the live session with no new pane); worktrees (W8: fork into a managed worktree launched on tmux with `--fork-session`, the Worktrees view showed it live, reopen attached to it, shell view printed WORKTREE_SHELL_VIEW in the worktree); plans (W9: Plans view listed demo-plan and its editor ran in place); overview (W12); ASL (W10: a real `asl run` started inside a tmux session put Working and the loop marker on that row only, the Runs view showed the run 'running' with 'binding: alpha', Enter on it attached to the hosting session, and the daemon state query tied that runtime session's slot to the run ID with kitty_snapshot.ready=false). The same binding is asserted against the installed asl in session-11/asl-integration-v.log (OBSERVED dashboard-binding; TestInstalledBridge* pass). Narrow/wide layout: the three new portable_tmux scenarios (140x36 and 80x24) and all 160 committed scenarios pass via `go run . tui-test run docs/tui-testing/scenarios/*.json`.
